purpose: Teach: 裏面/デタラメ/マズイ/酔っ払い/いまひとつ/合掌/かみさん/無茶苦茶

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが葉書の裏面に詩を書かれた
lines.en: You know, Gran — when your father was young, he'd write poetry on the back of postcards.
lines.style: Soft, remembering voice. Gentle opening. Pace slows as he moves into the memory. Trailing reverence at the end, like he's still seeing it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、デタラメな噂を信じない方だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He did, dear — and your grandfather, he was never one to believe idle gossip, was he?
lines.style: Warm affirmation, gentle redirection. Leans into the question at the end—not challenging, but gently steering him toward what matters. Soft emphasis on the loyalty.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがマズイご飯でも文句なく食べられた
lines.en: Gran, when he was young — your father would eat even a terrible meal without a single complaint.
lines.style: Same wistful pull as before. Slight wonder in the voice—a man astonished by kindness he'd taken for granted. Soft fade on the image.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、酔っ払いの客を諭された日もあったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: That's right, dear — and your grandfather, he'd talk sense into drunk customers some nights. Gently, never harsh.
lines.style: Nodding recognition. A small laugh beneath the words—fondness for that quiet strength. Patient rhythm, like she's watched him do this a hundred times.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、新事業がいまひとつ伸びなかった年もあった
lines.en: Gran, there were years when the new business didn't quite grow the way we hoped.
lines.style: Slight heaviness here—admission of old worry. The voice steadies though, like he's moving toward something beyond regret. Measured pace.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ご先祖様に毎朝合掌されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: But your grandfather, he bowed to his ancestors every morning, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Quiet certainty. A statement disguised as a question. Reverent but not sentimental—matter-of-fact about what prayer meant. Slight settling in the voice.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お父さんは私をかみさんと愛らしく呼んで下さった
lines.en: Gran, your father — he called me by such an affectionate name. Like I was his dear wife.
lines.style: Voice softens almost to a whisper. Affection and old wonder mixed together. Breathiness on the opening. Lingers on the word choice—it meant something specific.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、無茶苦茶な仕事もこなされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather, he tackled the craziest, most impossible work—and he simply did it. Without complaint.
lines.style: Quiet admiration settling over the words. Close, intimate, like she's telling him something he already knows but needs to hear again. Slight warmth at the close.
